paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of edits and both efficacy and noise for different editing methods. The x-axis is labeled "edits" and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 3000, with tick labels every 500. The left y-axis is labeled “Efficacy<sub>top</sub>” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick labels every 10. The right y-axis is labeled “noise<sub>ε</sub>” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140, with tick labels every 20. 

A red dashed line with square markers represents AlphaEdit Efficacy<sub>top</sub>, beginning at approximately 92 at x=0, declining to approximately 87 at x=3000. A light blue dashed line with square markers represents MEMIT Efficacy<sub>top</sub>, starting at approximately 82 at x=0 and decreasing to approximately 74 at x=3000. A red solid line with circular markers represents AlphaEdit noise<sub>ε</sub>, starting at approximately 14 at x=0 and increasing to approximately 18 at x=3000. A light blue solid line with circular markers represents MEMIT noise<sub>ε</sub>, starting at approximately 30 at x=0, peaking at approximately 140 at x=3000.
